title: Swift
label: Swift
desc: Apple's compiled language for iOS, macOS and server work, built on value types and safe optionals.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install the compiler on macOS or Linux and run a first executable.

snippets.code:
# macOS: the compiler ships with the command line tools
xcode-select --install
swift --version

# Linux: install the official toolchain manager, then a toolchain
curl -O https://download.swift.org/swiftly/linux/swiftly-x86_64.tar.gz
tar zxf swiftly-x86_64.tar.gz
./swiftly init

# Create a package and run it
swift package init --type executable
swift run
swift build -c release

sections.title: Syntax
sections.description: Bindings, interpolation and the control-flow forms used every day.

snippets.code:
// Constants and variables
let maximumAttempts = 3
var attempts = 0
attempts += 1

// Inferred and explicit types, then interpolation
let ratio: Double = 0.75
let name = "Felipe"
print("\(name): \(attempts)/\(maximumAttempts) attempts, \(Int(ratio * 100))%")

// Multi-line strings keep their indentation relative to the closing quotes
let banner = """
Retry limit: \(maximumAttempts)
Progress: \(Int(ratio * 100))%
"""
print(banner)

sections.title: Types
sections.description: Primitive values, tuples, explicit conversions and safe downcasting.

snippets.code:
let population: Int = 8_100_000
let pi: Double = 3.14159
let ready: Bool = true
let city: String = "Sao Paulo"
let initial: Character = "S"

// Tuples group values without declaring a type
let coordinate = (lat: -23.55, lon: -46.63)
print("\(city): \(coordinate.lat), \(coordinate.lon)")

// Numeric conversion is always explicit
let whole = Int(pi)
let scaled = Double(population) * 1.5
typealias Meters = Double
let distance: Meters = 42.0
print(whole, scaled, distance)

sections.title: Collections
sections.description: Arrays, dictionaries and sets with the usual transforms.

snippets.code:
var ages = ["ana": 31, "bruno": 24]
ages["carla"] = 45
ages["bruno"] = nil            // removes the entry
ages["ana"] = 32

for (name, age) in ages.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }) {
    print("\(name): \(age)")
}

// Default value avoids an optional result
print(ages["zoe", default: 0])

var visits: [String: Int] = [:]
visits["home", default: 0] += 1
print(visits)

let first: Set<String> = ["swift", "rust", "go"]
let second: Set<String> = ["go", "python"]

print(first.union(second).sorted())
print(first.intersection(second))
print(first.subtracting(second).count)
print(first.isSuperset(of: second))

let prices = [19.9, 5.0, 42.5, 8.25]
let expensive = prices.filter { $0 > 10 }
let withTax = expensive.map { $0 * 1.2 }
print(expensive.count, withTax.reduce(0, +))

let byLength = Dictionary(grouping: ["one", "two", "three"], by: \.count)
print(byLength[3]?.sorted() ?? [])
